title: Lena and the Summer
premise: Juniper Sterling returns to Saltmere Point to settle her late grandfather's estate, only to find the deed to his stubborn apple orchard lists two names: hers and Theo Marsh, the boy who left her twelve years ago without a word. The orchard cannot be sold or divided unless both heirs sign, forcing the estranged pair into a summer of shared labor, old letters, and a lighthouse log that reveals their grandparents once loved each other just as badly. As Juniper's editor deadline collides with the harvest, she must choose between the containable heart she's built and the whole, untrainable one Theo is asking for; they sign the deed together, keeping the orchard, and each other.
about_author: Vesper Nakamura is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who now writes coastal romances from a drafty cottage in Maine. Her novels are known for salt-weathered settings, stubborn inheritances, and hearts that refuse to stay organized.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Juniper arrives at Saltmere Point to settle her grandfather's estate and discovers the orchard deed names both her and Theo Marsh, the boy who vanished twelve years ago. Her POV. The beat is shock braided with old resentment, and the first crack in her belief that hearts can be managed.

chapters.title: Salt in the Margins
chapters.summary: Juniper drafts a rejection letter to the co-heir but can't finish it; instead she rereads her half-finished novel and finds Theo written into every love interest. Her POV. The beat is reluctant self-recognition, the writer confronting how much of her fiction is memory.

chapters.title: The Man at the Gate
chapters.summary: Theo appears at the orchard gate with his own lawyer's letter and a plan to sell fast. His POV reveals he never stopped thinking of her, and that his departure hid a family debt and shame. The beat is guarded tension, two people negotiating a fence line that used to be a friendship.

chapters.title: Terms of Harvest
chapters.summary: Their lawyers force a compromise: work the orchard together through harvest, then decide the sale. Juniper proposes it to keep control; Theo accepts to stay near her. Alternating POV. The beat is wary truce, the first fragile contract between old wounds and new proximity.

chapters.title: Ladder Work
chapters.summary: Pruning and ladder repairs put them shoulder to shoulder; a fall leaves Juniper bruised and Theo catching her. Her POV. The beat is the body remembering before the mind consents, desire surfacing through muscle memory she can't train away.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Log
chapters.summary: Juniper finds her grandfather's lighthouse logbook and discovers entries about a woman named Ada Marsh, Theo's grandmother, and a love the two old men never spoke of. Her POV. The beat is wonder and unease: the past is rhyming, and the orchard may be an inheritance of unfinished feeling.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: At the harborside diner, gossips fill in the story: Theo's father ruined the Marsh name and left overnight, and Theo took the blame going with him. His POV. The beat is humiliation and the weight of inherited identity, a man defined by a father's exit.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: A summer gale forces them to batten the orchard and the lighthouse shed together through one long wet night. Alternating POV. The beat is forced intimacy, laughter breaking through, and the almost-kiss both of them pretend didn't happen.

chapters.title: The Containable Heart
chapters.summary: Juniper's editor calls: the novel is due in six weeks, and it needs an ending she doesn't have. She tells Theo, flatly, that she doesn't do whole hearts, only loans. Her POV. The beat is self-sabotage, the narrator lying to herself in real time.

chapters.title: Letters in the Wall
chapters.summary: Repairing the cider house wall, Theo uncovers a tin of letters between his grandmother Ada and Juniper's grandfather, decades of devotion interrupted by one cruel season. His POV. The beat is grief and hope entangled, proof that their families' story is not the one the town told.

chapters.title: Cider and Confession
chapters.summary: Pressing the first cider, Theo tells Juniper why he really left: his father's debts, a threat against her family, a promise extracted by his dying mother. Her POV. The beat is the ground shifting, anger losing its footing against twelve years of misunderstood silence.

chapters.title: The Buyer from Away
chapters.summary: A developer offers a sum that could erase both their troubles, pressing for signatures before harvest's end. Theo, still ashamed, secretly considers taking it and leaving her free. His POV. The beat is temptation as self-erasure, the old reflex to disappear dressed up as generosity.

chapters.title: Deadline and Deadwood
chapters.summary: Juniper's manuscript stalls; she writes her heroine walking away and hates it. Meanwhile she finds Theo's copy of her first novel, annotated with devotion in the margins. Her POV. The beat is devastating tenderness, discovering she was loved through every year of silence.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: At the lighthouse at dusk, the kiss finally happens, and Juniper panics, invoking the sale timeline and retreating to the house. Alternating POV. The beat is joy curdling into fear, both of them realizing the stakes are now the whole heart, not pieces.

chapters.title: Ada's Last Letter
chapters.summary: The tin's final letter, never sent, reveals Ada waited at the orchard gate one autumn night and her grandfather never came, and why: a lighthouse rescue, a drowned boat, a promise made to the dead. Juniper's POV. The beat is sorrow as inheritance, the cost of a heart kept containable too long.

chapters.title: Signing Away
chapters.summary: Theo signs the sale agreement alone at the lawyer's office, choosing to free Juniper from the orchard and from him, and mails her his half. His POV. The beat is sacrifice mistaken for kindness, the novel's darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Unsent Chapter
chapters.summary: Juniper receives the signed deed and the annotated novel together, understands what Theo's leaving means, and burns her manuscript's ending, deciding to write the true one instead. Her POV. The beat is fury transfigured into resolve, the writer seizing her story back.

chapters.title: Race the Tide
chapters.summary: Juniper drives through a rising storm to stop the sale, while Theo, at the ferry dock, reads her manuscript pages she's slipped into his bag. Alternating POV. The beat is headlong pursuit, both racing the tide and their own inherited patterns.

chapters.title: The Orchard Gate
chapters.summary: She reaches him at the gate where Ada once waited; Theo tears up the agreement, confessing he'd rather lose everything than leave her a second time. His POV. The beat is the climax's release, the whole heart risked aloud, no more loans.

chapters.title: Harvest
chapters.summary: They sign a new deed, jointly holding the orchard, and bring in the harvest with the whole town, the first crop the families have shared in sixty years. Alternating POV. The beat is communal joy, private wounds made public and healed in daylight.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Juniper delivers her finished novel, now titled for the summer itself, and reads her grandfather's final log entry: a blessing on whoever the orchard kept together. Her POV. The beat is quiet fulfillment, memory and identity reconciled on the page.

chapters.title: Light On
chapters.summary: One year later: the lighthouse lamp relit as a memorial, the orchard bearing a new hybrid apple named for Ada and the old keeper, Theo and Juniper married beneath the trees. Her POV. The epilogue beat is inheritance fulfilled, love as the thing that was always meant to be kept, not contained.
